GAPS_SUMMARY: No FE/UI child story exists to anchor end-user acceptance steps directly. AC is primarily backend-oriented and technical; business checks are inferred from epic intent (reservation expires after 24h and stock becomes purchasable by others). Concrete test data for near-expiry reservations and cross-brand SKU setup must be prepared before execution.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: A reservation that passes its 24-hour validity window is no longer treated as active
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Use a product with a known reservation that is close to expiry in acceptance. Confirm the reservation is active before expiry and check again after the 24-hour mark or with a prepared expired fixture.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
After expiry threshold, reservation is no longer active for that customer.
System behavior reflects expired state consistently on re-check.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: Stock held by an expired reservation becomes available for another customer journey
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: After confirming an expired reservation case, attempt the same product flow with a different eligible customer/session. Validate that the item can be added/purchased where previously blocked by reservation hold.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
Previously held stock is available to another customer flow after expiry.
No persistent hold remains once reservation has expired.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: An expired reservation cannot proceed as if still valid
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Use an expired reservation scenario and continue through the checkout path where reservation validity is enforced. Observe behavior at the point reservation status is checked.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
Checkout does not continue under an expired reservation as valid.
User flow shows consistent handling of expired-state guardrail.

CHECKLIST_ROWS.Check: Reservation-expiry outcome behaves consistently across NAP and MRP acceptance
CHECKLIST_ROWS.How to Verify: Repeat one expired-reservation and one post-expiry stock-availability scenario on both NAP and MRP acceptance environments using equivalent setup data.
CHECKLIST_ROWS.Pass Criteria:
Expiration outcome is consistent on NAP and MRP.
Post-expiry availability behavior is consistent on NAP and MRP.

EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Summary: Implementation notes indicate scheduler/processing design choices evolved during delivery (delay queue assumptions vs scheduler approach).
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.How to Validate: During outcome testing, run the same expiry scenario twice with different processing windows to ensure no inconsistent expiry behavior appears due to scheduling cadence.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Expected Observation: Outcome remains deterministic: once expired, reservation remains expired and stock release behavior is consistent.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Impact: Scheduler edge behavior could create intermittent customer-facing inconsistency around the expiry boundary.

EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Summary: Attached ADR references concurrency considerations for reservation expiration worker behavior.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.How to Validate: Execute two close-timing expiry cases for similar products/customers and compare that outcomes are stable with no duplicate or conflicting release effects.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Expected Observation: No duplicate-release side effects and no conflicting reservation state presented to business users.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Impact: Concurrency anomalies could create brief stock/state confusion and reduce trust in reservation fairness.
EXPLORATORY_ROWS.Evidence Notes: ADR-Two-phase-reservation-expiration attachment noted in Jira; used as exploratory risk context only.
